latest.summary: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. items.title: BrainPFN: Amortized Brain-Behaviour Prediction via Prior-Data Fitted Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.06934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The standard approach to predicting behavioral phenotypes from functional MRI is represented by Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) applied on functional connectivity (FC) matrices. However, this approach is limited: separate models must be fit and tuned for every score and cohort, they do not transfer across datasets, and accuracy degrades sharply when only a handful of subjects are available, as is typical of clinical or cognitive studies. Despite an increasing interest in developing brain foundation models, none has consistently outperformed KRR on behaviour prediction; most reported gains come from easier targets such as age, sex, or diagnosis…

items.title: Patient-level validation of a foundation-model pipeline for pediatric lung sounds: physician-annotated adventitious events are recognized, disease groups are not reliably predicted
items.summary: Abstract Background Lung-sound classifiers are usually evaluated on recording- or event-level splits, although each child contributes many recordings. We evaluated a foundation-model pipeline (PulmoVec) with the patient as the unit of partitioning and asked whether disease group can be predicted beyond age and sex. Methods We analyzed 19693 physician-annotated respiratory events from 736 children in the public SPRSound database. A frozen Health Acoustic Representations encoder with low-rank adapters was trained for screening (normal versus adventitious), sound pattern (normal, crackles, wheeze/rhonchi) and disease group (pneumonia, bronchial disease, normal/other); event probabilities were…

items.title: Two Worlds, One Challenge: How AI Solves Unfamiliar Problems — Evidence from ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3

We examine two bounded studies of existing ARC solvers rather than equate intervention execution with success. In a Qwen3-based port of NVARC for static ARC-AGI-2, an updating configuration exceeded a zero-learning-rate configuration by 21.39 and 20.98 rounded public-score points in initial and repeated evaluations. In interactive ARC-AGI-3, recovery telemetry establishes that context-rebuilding interventions executed and were followed by environment actions, but not that they improved outcomes. items.title: Can Scalar-Field Memory Feed Back on Its Own Writing? An Order-of-Magnitude Feedback Estimate for the B3 Model
items.summary: The main paper showed that a two-field scalar model (B3) can hold localized, history-dependent records in halos, and that halo formation may make those records observationally uninformative. Here we ask the next question: could a stored record modify its own local gravitational environment? Using the frozen B3 model and its held-out synthetic halo population, we estimate three feedback channels without new field evolution. Under a heuristic, approximately isothermal halo response, a record deepens its own fifth-force well, so the core becomes denser and the record moves away from its erase threshold. We compare this density response with each halo’s erase margin. The response is smaller…

Second, a PD controller based on quaternion and angular velocity error feedback is designed to achieve the desired attitude necessary for the energy transmission…

items.title: Synaptic Multi-Weight Wafer-Scale Domain Wall Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Driven by Spin Orbit Torque
items.summary: Spintronic synaptic devices based on magnetic random access memory (MRAM) are a rapidly evolving class within the analog neuromorphic architecture. However, obtaining the multi-weight or analog behavior desired for improved neural network inference accuracy in scaled MRAM remains a challenge. In this study, we demonstrate and tune up to eight distinct resistance levels in 300 mm wafer-scale magnetic tunnel junction artificial synapses driven by spin orbit torque. By varying the applied in-plane field, multi-weight resistance states emerge through domain wall nucleation and pinning. These multi-weight states appear stochastically and can be addressed with an iterative programming algorithm…

items.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
items.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. We present SLA, a Spatial-Language-Action Model that scales implicit spatial alignment to continual pre-training and maintains it during downstream post-training. Initialized from a pretrained pi05 policy, SLA jointly optimizes…

items.title: OraRefer: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Photograph Fusion for Oral Cancer Screening with Guaranteed Patient-Level Sensitivity
items.summary: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs. However, screening refers patients, not photographs: a patient is usually photographed several times, and the referral decision must miss no more than a set share of patients with disease. We propose OraRefer, a patient-level screening model that reads each photograph with a segmentation-guided foundation model that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion, combines all photographs of a patient with risk factors, and refers…

items.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
items.summary: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. items.title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?
items.summary: sEMG Foundation Models aim to learn general purpose representations over diverse subjects and recording conditions that boost performance on a variety of downstream tasks. However, existing evaluations make it difficult to discern whether pretraining alone is sufficient to combat the cross-subject overfitting which makes machine learning on sEMG so challenging. We conduct a systematic evaluation of three sEMG foundation models across three gesture classification datasets under both intra-session and inter-subject splits, using three fine-tuning strategies designed to isolate the contribution of pretraining. We find that pretraining boosts performance when train and test samples are drawn…

items.title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
items.summary: Tokamak experiments record diverse measurements, including waveforms, profiles, fields, and scalars, which are used to reconstruct the plasma, forecast its evolution, recover associated control signals, and estimate disruption risk. Most models are built separately for one task and a fixed set of inputs and outputs, and each relies on a prescribed subset of diagnostics rather than structuring the full multimodal observation set to extract global, cross-signal information about the discharge. These limitations motivate a reusable foundation model that adapts to each task's input-output schema and models heterogeneous target signals jointly, rather than retraining a separate model for every…

items.title: Who Can Evaluate AI Independently? A Framework for Analysing Evaluation Infrastructure
items.summary: AI evaluation is increasingly central to AI safety and governance, yet taking part in an evaluation does not by itself confer authority over its design, its execution or the resources it depends on. This paper examines how infrastructure arrangements distribute that authority, and so shape who can evaluate AI systems independently. Drawing on Science and Technology Studies, political economy and applied evaluation standards, we introduce PAAI (Power, Access, Adequacy, Independence), a framework for examining who controls evaluation infrastructure, the terms on which it is available, whether it is adequate to the evaluation's purpose and what autonomy it supports. We apply PAAI to twelve…

items.title: Route-DMD: Distribution Matching Distillation with Task-Routed Mechanism for Speech Foundation Models
items.summary: Speech foundation models built on flow matching handle generation, editing, and processing in one system, but every request costs 20-50 iterative steps, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) doubles each of them. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) trains a student that approaches the teacher's quality in a few steps, yet existing speech distillation work applies it to generation alone. We show that a distribution-matching objective does not serve every task: in separation, the noised states of erroneous student outputs deviate far from the teacher's training distribution, where its prediction is unreliable. Route-DMD therefore makes the objective task-dependent, routing the affected…

items.title: When GeoFMs Meet VHR: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Very High Resolution Earth Observation Imagery
items.summary: Geospatial foundation models are a widely adopted starting point for remote sensing tasks. Most are pretrained on Sentinel-1/2 and Landsat imagery at a ground sampling distance (GSD) of 10m or coarser. Many applications instead rely on very high resolution (VHR) imagery, where individual buildings, roads, and amenities are resolved. We study which pretraining regimes transfer well to this scale. We introduce VHR-Bench, a benchmark suite of ten datasets at 1.5m GSD or finer spanning five task families, eight application domains, and both satellite and aerial platforms. We evaluate twelve encoders in three pretraining tiers with frozen backbones at two training-data fractions. We find that…

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and…

items.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
items.summary: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary…

items.title: When, Where, How: Active In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) adapt to a new task only through the labeled rows in their context. However, labels are expensive to acquire in real-world scenarios due to the need for highly specific domain knowledge to ensure high-quality data. Active in-context learning transfers classical acquisition rules to this setting, in which the model that guides acquisition changes with every label added. We ask how the value of diversity, predictive uncertainty and target-aware information gain changes as a frozen TFM acquires more context. For that, we study Target-Aware Nearest Neighbor (TANN) acquisition and the Expected Predictive Information Gain in Context (EPIC) and evaluate them…

items.title: InnerLogic-Surg: An Open Surgical Foundation Model via Continual Pretraining
items.summary: Vision foundation models are the backbone of modern surgical image analysis, yet most surgical systems still rely on encoders pretrained on natural images or on specialist models trained from scratch on comparatively small datasets. Pretraining encoders on large amounts of surgery-specific data has the potential to generally enhance the performance of surgical image analysis methods simply by providing stronger backbones. Here we present InnerLogic-Surg, an open family of surgical vision encoders (21M--300M parameters) obtained by continually pretraining a transformer-based image encoder on millions of surgical images curated from 11,965 internet-sourced surgical videos spanning ~2,900…

items.title: Responsible GenAI Use During Active Armed Conflict: Evidence from Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms
items.summary: Armed conflict can increase the value of Generative AI (GenAI) while undermining the conditions required for its responsible use. Yet the perspectives of community-based humanitarian responders working under these conditions remain underrepresented in responsible AI research. We examine GenAI use in Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs), a community-led humanitarian network, through an exploratory survey of 89 respondents and 15 semi-structured interviews with GenAI users and non-users. War reconfigures GenAI's role, making it most useful where its outputs are hardest to verify. ERR responders turned to GenAI when conflict made human expertise difficult or dangerous to reach. However,…

items.title: Scenario-aware Adaptive Neuromorphic Intelligence for multimodal sensor fusion
items.summary: Multisensory Physical AI systems operating in isolated conditions must make timely and reliable decisions within strict energy and hardware budgets. In this context, the present analytical study investigates the feasibility of reliable multimodal sensor fusion using a neuromorphic approach based on memristor-based Integrate-and-Fire neuron circuits driven by aggressively compressed representations of sensory information. Rather than relying on fixed processing and learning parameters, the proposed framework introduces scenario-dependent adaptability into individual stages of the neuromorphic decision-making pipeline, including sensor-data compression, nonlinear spike encoding, reliability…

items.title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
items.summary: Energy forecasting models are usually compared on backtests and fixed public datasets. Backtests can use data that did not yet exist when the forecast would have been made, and a fixed test set, reused across studies and possibly contained in the pretraining data of foundation models, invites overfitting to the benchmark. EnergyBench evaluates every entry live instead. Each day at 11:30 CET/CEST, thirty minutes before the day-ahead (SDAC) gate closes, every model forecasts the next day's price, wind and solar generation and load on the 15-minute grid for six bidding zones (BE, NL, FR, DE-LU, DK1, DK2). Unlike existing live benchmarks, EnergyBench runs the models itself, on one information…

items.title: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation
items.summary: Pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation is complicated by age-dependent electrophysiological changes that limit direct transfer of adult AI models. We asked whether an adult ECG foundation model could be adapted to pediatric ECGs. Using 339,563 12-lead ECGs from 238,189 children, we compared direct application, pediatric fine-tuning, and training from scratch under an identical architecture. Direct transfer was poor (mean AUC 0.8256). Fine-tuning reached 0.9695, above de novo training (0.9661), and attained 0.9079 using only 1% of training data. On 10,999 external ECGs, fine-tuning achieved a mean AUC of 0.9385 across 30 labels. It generalized to age regression (MAE 1.12 years)…

items.title: Real-Time Event-Based LED Tracking and Pose Estimation with PWM-Encoded Markers
items.summary: Event cameras are neuromorphic vision sensors with pixels that independently and asynchronously respond to brightness changes at microsecond resolution, supporting state estimation under rapid motion, motion blur, and high dynamic range (HDR) illumination. This also enables capture of high-frequency blinking patterns from light-emitting diodes (LEDs). Based on this, we propose a real-time event-based framework for LED tracking and six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) relative pose estimation using pulse-width modulation (PWM)-encoded LED markers. Multiple LEDs share a common blinking frequency and encode identities through distinct PWM duty cycles, reducing frequency-resource requirements and…

items.title: Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities
items.summary: Agent exploration produces valuable procedural knowledge, yet much of this experience remains confined to transient execution traces and is not systematically reused. We introduce Evolver, an experience-driven framework that transforms agent exploration into persistent, reusable capabilities without updating foundation model parameters. Built around structured Gene assets, Evolver integrates experience acquisition, retrieval, and feedback-guided evolution to support experience-conditioned execution across existing agent harnesses. We evaluate Evolver using Claude Code and Codex, two foundation model configurations, and four benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Multilingual,…

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
items.summary: Long-horizon role-playing dialogue requires consistent character identity, reliable memory, and context-sensitive interaction. We present a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework that revises original-character memory, stable persona instructions, and a policy for constructing turn-level prompts. Repair outcomes also inform revisions to the updater's diagnostic rules, edit routing, and candidate selection. We specify the updater as a versioned policy with explicit inputs, editable fields, acceptance gates, and stopping conditions. An internal evaluation covers 50 original characters and five models, with two 100-round conversations per character-model pair: 500 conversations…

items.title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
items.summary: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for vision and natural language. Moreover, they often require fixed input length and sampling rate, and generalize poorly to unseen sensor locations. items.summary: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. items.title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
items.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) shows that language models can reason about and rewrite neural network weights; recursive self-improvement (RSI) motivates feedback-driven improvement. Models guiding experiments receive concrete feedback: completed assays reveal prediction errors and inform what to test next. We introduce WeightLoop, a framework that turns experimental feedback into persistent updates to deployed predictors. GPT-6 Astra inspects a task specification and the model implementation, then writes a bounded, reusable parameter-editing program. items.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
items.summary: EHR foundation models read medical events within a fixed context window, and long context has so far been measured only in tokens. How far back in time a model must look to capture the earliest predictive signal is unknown. We introduce time-context, the calendar lookback window before the prediction point, and provide, to our knowledge, the first systematic evaluation of decade-scale time-context for an EHR foundation model. items.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

items.title: Medical superintelligence: foundations and aspirations.
items.summary: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have stimulated discussions about medical superintelligence , yet how to define and evaluate this aspiration remains unclear.
